walkthroughs.body_html:
Inorganic Chemistry — a core area of A-Level Chemistry.

Working through it builds the schema you need: the key terms, how they connect, and how to use them together.

Inorganic Chemistry brings together several ideas you need to use as a set, not in isolation.

Lock in the vocabulary first, then practise pulling the ideas together to answer real questions.

Use the activities in this adventure to build familiarity with Inorganic Chemistry.

Practise vocabulary, calculations and free-text questions to lock in the learning.

mcqs.q: Members of a homologous series share:
options: The same molecular mass
The same functional group and general formula
The same boiling point
The same number of isomers

mcqs.q: What kind of bond forms between a ligand and a central metal ion in a complex?
options: A dative (coordinate) covalent bond — the ligand donates a lone pair into an empty orbital on the metal.
The ligand forms an ionic bond with the metal because the metal is positively charged.
Mass is spread evenly throughout the entire atom including the electron shells.
The ligand shares electrons equally with the metal as a normal covalent bond.

mcqs.q: Where is almost all the mass of an atom located?
options: The ligand shares electrons equally with the metal as a normal covalent bond.
In the nucleus, made up of protons and neutrons.
Mass is spread evenly throughout the entire atom including the electron shells.
Electrons contribute significantly to the mass of an atom.

mcqs.q: When you reverse a reaction in a Hess cycle, what happens to ΔH?
options: ΔH becomes zero because the change cancels out.
Its sign reverses — if the forward reaction is +100 kJ/mol, the reverse is -100 kJ/mol.
The ligand shares electrons equally with the metal as a normal covalent bond.
ΔH stays the same because it's the same reaction.
